cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). He's been talking about his own people, Israel, and how not all of them welcomed the good news (Romans 10:16). So now he asks it straight out: 'I ask then, did God reject His people?'

cards.question: True or false: Paul answers that yes, God has rejected His people Israel.
Paul says CERTAINLY NOT, then points to himself as an Israelite and a descendant of Abraham, Israel's forefather. Which tribe is Paul from?

cards.text: Paul's out here using his own family tree as EXHIBIT A! He says God did not reject His people, whom He foreknew.
Then Paul brings up Elijah, a prophet (1 Kings 18:36), and how Elijah appealed to God against Israel. Elijah says, 'Lord, they have killed Your prophets and torn down Your altars.'

cards.question: Elijah tells God that His prophets are killed and His altars are torn down. Then he tells God who's left. What does Elijah say?

answers.text: He is the only one left

cards.text: Elijah adds that they are seeking his life as well. I think he feels all alone, friend.

cards.question: Paul asks what the divine reply to Elijah was. God says, 'I have reserved for Myself seven thousand men…' What makes those seven thousand stand out?

answers.text: They never bowed to the false god Baal
They hid all of God's true prophets
They rebuilt all of God's torn altars

cards.question: True or false: God's reply means Elijah was not the only one left who hadn't bowed the knee to Baal.

cards.text: Elijah's story wasn't just a trip down memory lane, friend. Paul says it's the same way at the present time.

cards.question: Like the seven thousand in Elijah's day, Paul says there is something at the present time. What is it?

cards.text: Paul says this remnant is chosen by grace. Then he sets grace right next to works.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the remnant is chosen partly by grace and partly by works.

cards.text: Paul says if it's by grace, it's no longer by works, or grace would no longer be grace. Grace you earn isn't a gift, friend, that's a PAYCHECK!

cards.question: Paul asks, What then? True or false: Paul says Israel obtained what it was seeking.
Israel failed to obtain what it was seeking, but Paul says the ___ did.

cards.text: Seeking it and not getting it is like chasing a bus for three blocks and watching the doors close right in front of you. Paul says the others were hardened.
Paul backs that up with Scripture, drawing on Deuteronomy 29:4 and Isaiah 29:10: 'God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that could not see, and ears that could not hear…'

cards.question: The Scripture Paul quotes says God gave them eyes that could not see and ears that could not hear. How long does it say that lasts?

cards.text: Then Paul quotes David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), from Psalm 69:22-23: 'May their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution to them.' David goes on, 'May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.'

cards.question: True or false: David's line about eyes being darkened so they cannot see echoes the Scripture Paul quoted before it, about eyes that could not see.
